idea: Farmland carbon and biodiversity credit advisory
pain: Carbon and biodiversity credit schemes are confusing and easy to get wrong
v1: A credit opportunity assessment for one estate
channel: Italian agriculture contacts plus UK land contacts
verdict: Real tailwind and a genuine analytical gap, but she lacks agricultural and ecological credentials.

why.distribution: Landowners reachable through her husband's contacts, but scattered across two countries.
why.demand: Inferred; credit markets are immature and landowners are sceptical after several failed schemes.
why.fmf: Financial analysis transfers, but soil carbon and biodiversity assessment are technical fields she lacks.
why.defensibility: Accumulated scheme comparisons help; specialist ecologists compete.
why.tailwind: Nature and carbon credit regulation is expanding rapidly with real money behind it.
why.ceiling: £11k x 18 estates = £198k, requiring a landowner client base across two countries.

ceiling_arithmetic: £11k x 18 estates = £198k less technical subcontract ~30% = £139k. Reaching eighteen estate clients across two countries in year one is not plausible. Realistic: 3-4 = £23-31k net.
carries: One of the strongest regulatory tailwinds available and a genuine analytical gap.
kills: Credentials. Carbon and biodiversity assessment requires technical expertise she would have to buy.
test: Ask three landowners whether they have looked at credit schemes and what stopped them.
test_pass: They tried and could not evaluate the offers.
test_fail: They dismiss credits as a fad.
